source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Straight lines appearing wavy to an older adult suggests:
questions.rationale: Wet AMD: abnormal vessels leak under the retina, distorting central vision.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Macular Degeneration (PDF p. 479)
questions.quote: Patients report that straight lines appear crooked and distorted

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with macular degeneration is given an Amsler grid. The nurse instructs to:
options: Check one eye at a time weekly
questions.rationale: Check each eye several times weekly with glasses; report changes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, AMD Nursing (PDF p. 479)
questions.quote: look at these grids, one eye at a time, several times each week

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client has a metal fragment protruding from the eye. The nurse should:
options: Shield the eye, do not remove
questions.rationale: Never remove; protect with a metal shield or cup; no pressure.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Penetrating Injuries (PDF p. 480)
questions.quote: No attempt should be made to remove the foreign object

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A chemical splashes into a worker's eye. The first action is:
questions.rationale: Immediately irrigate with tap water or normal saline.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Splash Injury (PDF p. 480)
questions.quote: Eye should be immediately irrigated with tap water or normal saline

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Blood in the anterior chamber of the eye after trauma is called:
questions.rationale: Hyphema is hemorrhage within the chamber.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Contusion of the Eyeball (PDF p. 480)
questions.quote: Hyphema (hemorrhage within the chamber)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Enucleation of an irreparable injured eye is done within 2 weeks to prevent:
questions.rationale: Sympathetic ophthalmia can blind the uninjured eye.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Eye Trauma (PDF p. 480)
questions.quote: to prevent the risk of sympathetic ophthalmia

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A normal tympanic membrane appears:
questions.rationale: Normal TM is pearly gray and translucent.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ear Anatomy (PDF p. 480)
questions.quote: Normally pearly gray and translucent

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Pain when the auricle is pulled suggests:
questions.rationale: External otitis causes pain on auricle manipulation; mastoid tenderness suggests mastoiditis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Auditory Assessment (PDF p. 481)
questions.quote: External otitis is suspected if there is pain upon manipulation of the auricle

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: In conductive hearing loss, the Weber test lateralizes to the:
questions.rationale: Conductive: Weber to affected ear, bone > air on Rinne; sensorineural: Weber to better ear.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tuning Fork Tests (PDF p. 482)
questions.quote: hears the sound better in the affected ear

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A normal Rinne test shows:
questions.rationale: Normally air conduction is longer than bone conduction.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tuning Fork Tests (PDF p. 482)
questions.quote: air-conducted sound is louder than bone-conducted sound

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which teaching prevents otitis externa (swimmer's ear)?
questions.rationale: Avoid wetting and trauma; do not use cotton-tipped applicators.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Otitis Externa (PDF p. 482)
questions.quote: Instruct patients not to clean the external auditory canal with cotton-tipped applicators

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Meniere's triad consists of vertigo, tinnitus, and:
questions.rationale: Abnormal endolymph causes vertigo, tinnitus, and fluctuating sensorineural loss.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Meniere's Disease (PDF p. 483)
questions.quote: Meniere’s Triad

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During a vertigo attack from Meniere's disease, the client should:
options: Lie still in a safe place
questions.rationale: Lie down and stay still; recognize aura to prepare.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Meniere's Nursing (PDF p. 484)
questions.quote: Encourage patient to lie down during attack, in safe place, and lie still

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which diet modification helps Meniere's disease?
questions.rationale: Limit salt, sugar, and alcohol to stabilize inner ear fluid.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Meniere's Nursing (PDF p. 484)
questions.quote: Limit foods high in salt or sugar.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug is commonly used to control vertigo?
questions.rationale: Vestibular suppressants such as meclizine control vertigo.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Meniere's Management (PDF p. 483)
questions.quote: Meclizine (Antivert, Bonine) up to 25 mg qid

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An insect is lodged in a child's ear. The nurse should first:
questions.rationale: Irrigation is contraindicated for insects; mineral oil kills and dislodges it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Foreign Bodies (PDF p. 484)
questions.quote: Insect can be dislodged by instilling mineral oil

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Ear irrigation to remove cerumen is contraindicated with:
questions.rationale: Do not irrigate with a perforated drum or inflamed canal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Impacted Cerumen (PDF p. 484)
questions.quote: unless the patient has a perforated eardrum

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The intraoperative phase begins when:
options: Client is transferred to OR table
questions.rationale: Intraoperative: OR table transfer until PACU admission.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Perioperative Nursing (PDF p. 485)
questions.quote: Intraoperative phase begins when the patient is transferred onto the OR table

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Surgery for intestinal obstruction is classified as:
questions.rationale: Emergency surgery requires immediate attention.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Surgical Classifications (PDF p. 485)
questions.quote: Emergency – The situation requires immediate surgical attention without delay

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A gastrostomy tube for a client unable to swallow is which type of surgery?
questions.rationale: Palliative surgery relieves symptoms without curing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Surgical Classifications (PDF p. 485)
questions.quote: Palliative (eg, to relieve pain or correct a problem

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Who is responsible for obtaining informed surgical consent?
questions.rationale: The surgeon explains and obtains consent; the nurse may witness.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Informed Consent (PDF p. 485)
questions.quote: Consent is obtained by the surgeon.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is a responsibility of the circulating nurse?
questions.rationale: Circulator verifies consent, coordinates team, monitors asepsis, and does counts with the scrub nurse.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Surgical Team (PDF p. 485)
questions.quote: Verifying consent

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In which OR zone are masks required at all times?
questions.rationale: Restricted zone requires scrubs, caps, shoe covers, and masks.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Surgical Environment (PDF p. 486)
questions.quote: Restricted zone: scrub clothes, shoe cover caps, and masks are worn
